A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAVias and provide the main text, experiments, mathematical derivations, and appendices needed for comparison. V2's final tag table extends beyond the visible page, but its embedded text is recoverable, so this layout defect does not leave an evidence gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments on four image datasets, component ablations, and an appendix experiment using a biased two-moon distribution.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds open-set comparisons across three datasets and an evaluation of GPT-4o tag filtering against manually established ground truth.

M1.justification: The tagging, LLM filtering, vision-language encoding, additive-logit training, and inference procedures remain unchanged. V1's regularization term is renamed the logit alignment term in v2, with the same formula. More specific encoder names do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The four image datasets, seven ImageNet9 variants, and two-moon scenario remain. V2 presents its main CelebA task as hair-color prediction with gender bias, supported by blonde/non-blonde tag tables; v1 evaluates gender prediction with hair-color bias. That earlier task remains in v2 supplementary Table 13. The task descriptions are not clearly reconciled.

E2.justification: V2 adds SD and FLAC-B to the retained ImageNet9 comparison (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 3). Its new open-set comparisons also evaluate a common LfF, JTT, SD, Debian, and FLAC-B panel across three datasets, substantially broadening comparator participation. Earlier closed-set comparators, including SoftCon, DISC, and bias-aware methods, remain in the supplement.

E3.justification: V2 adds class-specific, tag-defined open-set evaluation: vanilla-model accuracy identifies biased tags, samples form two groups per class, and epochs are selected using overall accuracy without bias information (Section 4.4). ImageNet9 is exempted because some groups contain fewer than four samples. A separate new protocol measures tag-filter precision and recall against manual ground truth.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused GPT-4o filtering diagnostic (Table 9) and broader class-specific tag analyses, while removing v1's ImageNet9 aligned/conflicting case-study results (Table 6). Existing component ablations, projection-accuracy and vocabulary analyses, two-moon demonstration, and hyperparameter study are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use five different random seeds and retain the same plus/minus reporting practice (v1 Appendix A.2.2; v2 Section 4.3). Additional result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run policy, or significance test.

E6.justification: V2 Table 2 adds open-set worst-group/average accuracies of 66.7/81.4 for CelebA, 75.4/87.5 for Waterbirds, and 84.4/89.3 for UrbanCars; Table 9 adds filtering precision/recall. These are new-protocol results, not gains over v1's closed-set scores. MAVias's ImageNet9 scores remain unchanged, but added baselines alter margins: MIXED-NEXT is 88.26 versus SD's 87.56. V1's Table 6 subgroup results are removed.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A.1 and v2 Supplementary Section 1 retain the same gradient argument and unbiased-distribution/logit-addition derivation. Assumptions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged apart from numbering, notation, and terminology. The new grouping procedure is an evaluation protocol rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an instance-level open-set bias-identification framework and a foundation-model-assisted strategy for learning bias-invariant representations, with effectiveness across four datasets. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain this scientific scope; the new experiments principally add support for existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies sparse ImageNet9 tag-defined groups as an evaluation limitation, interprets additional dataset-specific bias patterns, and adds guidance about hyperparameter sensitivity in Supplementary Section 5. The gradient-starvation explanation and limitations concerning tagging vocabulary and sensitive-data applications largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds class-specific irrelevant-tag inventories for all four datasets (Tables 17–20), an implementation-availability statement naming VB-Mitigатор, baseline hyperparameters, and encoder variants such as OpenCLIP ViT-L-14. Most existing training details move into the main text. The reported ImageNet hardware also changes from RTX-4090 to A100; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused distinction between a priori instance-level filtering and validation-based discovery or subgroup mitigation, and revises the comparison with OpenBias. References add OpenCLIP, VB-Mitigатор, and several bias-related works, while replacing the original CLIP citation. The overall open-set research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized into separate dataset, architecture, implementation, protocol, comparison, and ablation sections. Existing appendix material moves into the main text, closed-set comparisons are condensed, and the appendix becomes separately structured supplementary material. Introduction and related-work passages are edited, with BLA/BLU and regularization terminology revised.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as a pipeline and Figure 2 is restyled. The dog-tag visualization is replaced by broader tag tables; new comparison and diagnostic tables are added, and closed-set results are consolidated and relocated. Typography and layout change throughout. V2 Table 20 overflows the final page, visibly clipping part of the Instrument and Primate lists.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central open-set claim, previously assessed largely through predefined-bias benchmarks, by adding tag-defined group comparisons across three datasets, stronger ImageNet9 comparators, and a manual-ground-truth check of tag filtering. Tag inventories and implementation information also improve scrutiny and reproducibility. Inconsistent CelebA task descriptions, stale introductory performance margins, and the clipped final table are drawbacks, but the gain in empirical support is substantial.
